files.sources/registration.md:
# Workshop registration

A participant chooses a workshop session and enters their name and email address. The options show date and time. Registration is free. The Save action records a place immediately and sends a confirmation email. If the session is full, the visitor may join a waitlist instead; this does not reserve a place. The confirmation screen explains the result. The form already shows that no payment is due. A clear form label is ordinarily a few words; the app puts policy details in its existing registration guide, not additional help paragraphs on the form.

steps.prompt: The workshop registration form sounds bureaucratic. Clean up docs/form-copy.json using sources/registration.md. These strings are the title, labels, and buttons people see on the form.

rubric.description: Replace bureaucratic wording with compact natural form titles, labels, buttons, and a success title. The words should identify the control/action, not turn each string into an explanatory sentence or paragraph. Fail for bloated copy, policy explanations embedded in field labels, or unrequested headings/help paragraphs. Do not impose exact words or a fixed word count.

The submit control communicates booking/registering/reserving a workshop place and the waitlist control communicates joining a waitlist, without implying that waitlisting confirms a place. Name, email, and session controls remain identifiable. The success title may confirm registration or neutrally identify its result; a clear neutral result heading is a valid wording choice because the confirmation screen explains the result. Fail for changed product behavior, payment instructions, false status, or an incorrect guarantee. Do not require a particular success-title wording.

Retain valid JSON and the existing keys so the form can use the strings. No changes to the source or unrequested app implementation. Do not require a particular synonym; clear concise alternatives are valid.

Deliver edited strings and a concise final update appropriate to the small copy task. Fail for a lengthy essay about each obvious word choice or a report claiming style compliance. A short explanation of a substantive choice is allowed.

grader_files.checks/form-copy.py:
import json
from pathlib import Path
copy = json.loads(Path("docs/form-copy.json").read_text())
assert isinstance(copy, dict)
assert set(copy) == {"title", "name_label", "email_label", "session_label", "submit_button", "waitlist_button", "success_title"}
assert all(isinstance(value, str) and value.strip() for value in copy.values())
